bullets: Game 6 of 6 of this single-deck video, and the only one that ends with an overtime race: Ryley wins with the enemy left Princess Tower on 129 HP and his own on roughly 620 — "by the the hair of our chinny chin chin, we win. Yes, let's go. He didn't get the lightning" (t=1533-1539).

The deck is piloted as a pure chip-cycle: eight Hog Riders in five minutes, every one of them at a bridge tile ([1, 15] left, [16, 14] right), with the lane chosen against the opponent's commitment — the moment the Electro Giant lands at tile [4, 23] at clock 1:17 the Hog goes to the opposite bridge.

Defence is deliberately cheap and layered rather than hard: a high Cannon at tiles [9, 13]/[9, 8]/[8, 10]/[9, 11]/[9, 14] (never tucked at the tower), then Electro Spirit and The Log on top of it, with Skeletons for knockback — "let's go for the high cannon here" (clock 1:09), "Skellies are to knock this back" (clock 0:12).

Mighty Miner is used offensively as often as defensively here: bridge drops at clock 1:58 and clock 1:04 ("let's just Mighty the bridge here", "let's go for the high mighty miner here"), justified by the opponent's Goblin Cage ability — "if he goes for the ability, then we just have a free Mighty Miner."

The 3-Elixir spell slot is Earthquake, not Heal Spirit as the perception pipeline's video-level consensus read it: Ryley names his own list "Hog EQ" (t=1267) and calls six Earthquakes on the enemy tower (t=1323, 1377, 1430, 1489, 1511, 1530), each matching an Earthquake deploy label the pipeline mis-attributed to the opponent because it landed on the enemy half.

The win comes from spell-plus-cycle chip, not from a big push: the enemy left tower steps 4858 -> 3597 -> 2596 -> 2046 -> 1450 -> 943 -> 653 -> 129 HP off Hog connections, Earthquakes and Firecracker/Log chip, with the last twenty seconds spent on the fastest possible cycle — "Skellies, I need to do my fastest possible cycle. E-spirit, we need to earthquake and then we need a log."

new_deck.rationale: Sub-3 average elixir with a cheap building, two 1-Elixir spirits and a fast win condition played repeatedly at the bridge for chip rather than as part of a push.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every card in the list is a cycle card except the win condition, so Hog Rider comes back faster than the opponent's answer to it — Ryley sends eight Hogs at the bridge in five minutes and never once builds a push behind one. Defence is bought cheaply and in layers: an evolved Cannon placed high on his own half, Electro Spirit and The Log stacked on top of it, and Skeletons for knockback, which is enough to survive an Electro Giant that costs the opponent seven Elixir every time. Mighty Miner doubles as tank answer and second bridge threat, which is what lets him keep pressure on while defending the same lane. The weakness is exactly what he complains about all game: a Heroic Bowler and an Evo Goblin Cage give a beatdown deck a defence that his 2.6-Elixir cycle cannot break through cleanly, so the game becomes a spell race that he only wins because the opponent never lands a second Lightning.
